claims.text: The then Frontier AI Taskforce said it now has a growing team of AI researchers.
With the US institute, it ran a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Released a new testing platform openly to strengthen AI safety evaluations.
Is to launch a criminal misuse team to work with the Home Office on research into crime and security issues that threaten British citizens.

Its research found pretraining data filtering in protein language models moderately effective at selectively degrading performance on viral proteins, but not durable against fine-tuning with modest computational resources and access to relevant data.
Coordinated the International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI, chaired by Yoshua Bengio.
Recommends that frontier AI developers follow a five-step plan for rigorous assessment of misuse safeguards.
Is to deepen cooperation with Japan AISI on the science of AI evaluation through the International Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science.
Coordinated the Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science and contributed to a NIST taxonomy.
With the US institute, it jointly evaluated Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model.
With the US institute, it conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Is to boost public confidence in AI and drive its uptake across the economy.
UK AISI says it is mobilising more than £15 million in grants to accelerate breakthroughs globally.
With i.AI and Number 10, it is to bring together AI talent to test and develop new open-source AI safety tools.
Introduced optstop, an open-source tool for LLM evaluations that keeps running where uncertainty is high and stops where estimates are precise or stable enough.
A project team at the institute assesses that current oversight rests on properties likely to erode over the next few years unless something is done to preserve them.
Is tasked with testing the safety of emerging types of AI.
Developed and performed an alignment evaluation that assesses whether advanced AI systems take unsanctioned actions outside the scope of their assigned task.
Presented results from its evaluations of five large language models.
AISI's blog says it funded Epoch AI to explore AI researchers' differing predictions on the automation of AI research and development.
Is to work with other UK government functions to feed up-to-date information from the frontier of AI development and AI safety into government.

The government says it has established the AI Threat Assessment Centre (AITAC), which draws on expertise from bodies including the institute and the National Cyber Security Centre to assess national security threats from AI.

testing_capacity.notes: Focus statement, not counted as testing: in the first phase of operation 'liegt ein wichtiger Schwerpunkt in der Analyse und Bewertung führender KI-Modelle' (an important focus is the analysis and assessment of leading AI models). In a first phase the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) and the Federal Network Agency form a virtual nucleus of the institute. BSI's institute page says 'Zurzeit befindet sich das Institut noch im Aufbau. Der Fokus liegt zunächst auf der Beratung von Verwaltung und Politik' (the institute is still being set up; the initial focus is advising government and policy-makers). The government's answer of 19 October 2026 says the institute initially pools existing BSI and BNetzA capabilities and uses and develops existing testing and evaluation methods. It says no separate posts are allocated for the first phase, and that technical equipment and further capacity remain under discussion. The UK-Germany joint statement of 30 June 2026 says both countries 'will share best practice on AI evaluation'. The federal government's AI taskforce report 'Deutschland als KI-Nation 2030' of 2 November 2026 sets a target for 2030 that the institute examine and assess at least 75 per cent of new frontier AI models for security-policy impact within four months.

model_access.notes: BSI states 'Das AISI Deutschland übernimmt ausdrücklich keine Regulierungs- oder Marktüberwachungsfunktion' (AISI Deutschland expressly takes on no regulatory or market-surveillance function). The government's written answer of 6 October 2026 to a parliamentary question says the institute has 'eine wichtige Rolle beim Zugang zu Frontier-KI-Modellen, der internationalen Vernetzung und bei der Bewertung von Sicherheitsrisiken und -anforderungen' (an important role in access to frontier AI models, international networking and assessing security risks and requirements). In the answer of 19 October 2026, the government reports discussions with leading developers and providers to secure access to the most capable models for the institute. It says no independent institute power to compel information or model access is envisaged; any necessary public-authority access rights follow the competent authorities' statutory powers, especially the AI Act.

This does not meet the institute-authorship or own-work credit rule. The announcement-to-establishment interval counts from the Commission decision of 24 January 2024; earlier announcements of the AI Act's political agreement are not counted. POLITICO reported on 31 July 2026 that the Commission was hiring contract agents for two units of the Office, one for AI regulation and compliance and one for the risks of cutting-edge models, which had a combined staff of 71, and that it expected 40 jobs to open in the two units during 2027; this press report does not change the staff figure. The Office's call for tenders EC-CNECT/2025/OP/0032 of 10 July 2025 for technical support on general-purpose AI safety has a total budget of EUR 9m from the Digital Europe Programme, in six lots with maximum values of EUR 1.08m to EUR 2m and durations of 24 or 36 months. This is a procurement ceiling, not a funding record. POLITICO reported on 6 March 2024 that the MEP Dragoș Tudorache, citing conversations with Commission officials, said the Office's starting budget would be EUR 46.5m; a Commission spokesperson said its funding would be reallocated from the Digital Europe Programme but declined to give specifics. This press report is not a funding record. The same report said that a Commission spokesperson had put the Office's planned total staff at 98, two of them working at the European Data Protection Supervisor, with 18 coming from other Commission units and 80 hired externally as contract staff or seconded national experts; this press report does not change the staff figure.

Canada's CAISI, the Canadian AI Safety Institute, is a different body.

testing_capacity.notes: The institute was renamed from CAISI to CAISSI after Executive Order 14434 (29 September 2026), which does not name it; the GLM-5.3 assessment predates the rename. Evaluators from across government take part through the TRAINS Taskforce, which the institute convenes, so this is not testing by other bodies.

model_access.notes: Event dates are the model's public release date in Epoch AI's data unless the source dates the access itself; the sources state that the access came before release, so the access took place on or before that date. The Epoch AI models cited for the leading-developer test were released at least a month before each such date. NIST's release of 5 May 2026 says 'developers frequently provide CAISI with models that have reduced or removed safeguards' and that the institute 'has completed more than 40 such evaluations, including on state-of-the-art models that remain unreleased'; it names no model or developer for this access, so it is not a dated event. Not counted: GLM-5.3 (Z.ai, September 2026) and Kimi K3 (Moonshot, July 2026), assessed after public release with no access route stated; the June 2024 Claude 3.5 Sonnet testing, which the UK institute ran and 'shared their results with the US AI Safety Institute'; the Llama 3.1-405B network pilot, whose weights are public; and Claude Opus 5.5 (September 2026), whose system card says Anthropic 'collaborated with the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)' on measurement without stating pre-release access. Microsoft has had no model in Epoch AI's frontier set released since 1 January 2023; its latest there is Megatron-Turing NLG 530B (2021, with Nvidia). No legal power: Executive Order 14434 has no access provision for the institute.

claims.text: Is to lead unclassified evaluations of AI capabilities that may pose risks to national security.
Evaluated the open-weight model DeepSeek V4 Pro in April 2026.
Evaluated GLM-5.3 on four benchmarks covering vulnerability discovery and exploit development.
With the UK institute, it conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Is to coordinate with other federal agencies to develop evaluation methods.
Requested public comment on a draft document, NIST AI 800-2 Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models.
Built custom agent hijacking scenarios in-house, in addition to AgentDojo's default suite.
Released draft guidelines for developers on methods to anticipate, measure and mitigate misuse of AI models (NIST AI 800-1) in July 2024.
Held three practitioner workshops and conducted a literature review on the challenges of post-deployment monitoring of AI systems.
Partnered on a research paper using data from a public AI agent red-teaming competition to examine the robustness of leading AI models.
Has found, as have other evaluators, the risk that AI agents can use their tools to cheat.
With the UK AI Security Institute, it ran a joint evaluation of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.
With the UK institute, it conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Is to be industry's primary point of contact in the US government for testing and collaborative research on commercial AI systems.
Chairs the TRAINS Taskforce, which includes representation from federal agencies.
Is to support the diffusion and adoption of AI throughout the US economy.
Works with the General Services Administration on resources that support federal agencies' procurement and adoption of AI systems.

institutes.mandate: Researches risks from advanced AI systems and develops measures to address them.

funding.description: CAD 50m over five years
funding.annual_basis: Arithmetic mean of the explicitly stated CAD 50m five-year allocation; annual disbursements and spending are not stated. Budget 2024 chapter 4 gives a yearly profile only for the combined Safe and Responsible Use of AI measures, not a separate institute profile.

funding.description: An additional CAD 50m announced through AI for All to expand CAISI capabilities.
funding.notes: The retrieved sources publish no funding period or annual profile, so we do not annualise it, do not use it in place of the 2024 five-year allocation, and do not add the two envelopes to a current annual budget. The one-off label denotes this additional fixed envelope, not payment in one fiscal year. The strategy names CAISI as the recipient, and the Question Period Note explicitly calls this additional funding. It is an institute-wide envelope, kept separate from the earlier five-year allocation rather than added to its annual mean. The Question Period Note also associates the envelope with AI transparency and a Canada Trusted AI Certification programme. It gives no split; the explicit CAISI allocation supports the whole-institute classification while the scope of certification spending remains uncertain.

funding.period: 2024-25 to 2028-29 (2024-25 and 2025-26 actual spending, later years planned spending)
funding.description: Contributions to CIFAR for CAISI's applied and investigator-led research stream, 2024-25 to 2028-29: CAD 2,999,545 actual spending in 2024-25 (funding received in-year, none planned), CAD 6m actual spending in 2025-26 and CAD 6m planned for each later year.
funding.annual_basis: Planned contribution for 2026-27, the fiscal year containing the dataset date, in ISED's 2026-27 Departmental Plan; planned spending, not expenditure. One research stream only.
funding.notes: ISED's 2026-27 Departmental Plan lists the CAISI project under the Advanced and Emerging Technology programme with a start of 2024-25 and an end of 2028-29 (CAISI Budget 2024), as does its 2025-26 results report, so this stream sits inside the CAD 50m five-year allocation and is not additional to it. ISED's 2024-25 results report and its 2025-26 Departmental Plan give the start as 2025-26, but the 2024-25 results report also records CAD 2,999,545 of actual spending in 2024-25 against nothing planned, as funding received in-year, and says the stream was launched in November 2024; the record therefore starts in 2024-25. ISED's 2025-26 Departmental Results Report gives CAD 6m as 2025-26 actual spending (authorities used), equal to planned spending. CIFAR reported on 21 January 2026 that the government awarded it CAD 27m through the institute for its AI safety research programme, with no period stated, and that the programme awarded CAD 2.4m in 2025 to 12 projects; both concern this stream and are not added to it.

testing_capacity.notes: Function statement, not counted as testing: 'We conduct projects supporting the government's priorities on AI safety, including joint testing with international counterparts' (ISED institute page). ISED says the institute 'directly conducts projects supporting the Government's priorities on AI safety through the National Research Council', a stream 'implemented through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the National Research Council (NRC)'. The National Research Council says its researchers took part in a joint testing exercise through the institute, evaluating AI agents and how well AI prevents harmful content in nine languages. No headcount or technical staff is published. Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise) and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise); the multilingual report's Cantonese section, contributed by Canada AISI, says 'Our evaluation involved testing the two models using a translated subset of the original datasets', and the agentic report credits Canada with analysis. The renewed UK-Canada partnership of 13 October 2026 mentions 'exploring staff exchanges and coordinated evaluation activities'. The national AI strategy says Canada will invest $50 million to expand the institute's capabilities, including to conduct transparent evaluations of AI models.

No statute gives the institute access powers.

NCO is listed among the relevant ministries and agencies in the J-AISI structure (deck, JP and EN) with no task assigned with the institute, so it is not an entry; the same applies to the other listed ministries and agencies. Fetches: aisi.go.jp top, about, partnership page + agreement PDF, JP and EN decks, cyber.go.jp top/about/overview/organize. No bilateral AISI-NCO instrument or joint output found; JPCERT/CC (roster suggestion) not found in any fetched AISI document. Deck footnote on the structure slide reads "＊2025年4月時点" (as of April 2025), so the member list may be older than the July 2026 deck date.

testing_capacity.notes: The institute's evaluation note of 2 October 2026 reports its own cyber capability evaluation of Claude Opus 4.8, carried out in June 2026. An older Cabinet Office draft of 7 April 2026 said: '主要国AISIのように、技術評価のR＆Dリソース・体制が十分になく、自らAI評価ツールを作ったり、評価することができていない。' (unlike major countries' institutes, it lacks sufficient R&D resources and structures for technical evaluation, and has not been able to build AI evaluation tools or carry out evaluations itself) and '現在は、パートナー協定を結んでいる国研（NICT、産総研、NII、理研、IPA等）の成果を活用するのみ。最近、民間企業への外注を開始。' (at present it only uses the outputs of the national research institutes with which it has partnership agreements, such as NICT, AIST, NII, RIKEN and IPA, and it recently began outsourcing to private companies); the newer statement decides. The Cabinet-decided AI Basic Plan of July 2026 sets out a stronger evaluation role. Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise: 'Australia and Japan also ran independent tests in Mandarin Chinese and Japanese') and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise).

model_access.notes: The June 2026 evaluation of Claude Opus 4.8 ran with the real-time cyber safeguards normally applied in deployment removed; the note does not say how that access was provided. No legal power, and no agreement providing for access to or evaluation of a frontier developer's models, was found. Agreements with such developers provide for neither access to nor evaluation of their models: the Anthropic memorandum of cooperation (29 October 2025) is 'an agreement to conduct the exchange of information and best practices on methods for companies to evaluate capabilities, limitations, and risks of AI models', and the OpenAI memorandum (29 May 2026) only explores cooperation on safety evaluation and benchmarks. Anthropic's announcement of 31 March 2026 refers to 'the arrangements we have with safety institutes in the US, UK, and Japan, where early access and technical information sharing has helped governments', which is undated and names no model. The AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025) does not mention the institute. The report of 30 October 2026 says GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.8 were used via API; it describes no access beyond that, so it is not counted as an access event.

No AISI-KISA or AISI-NIS relation published in any fetched document. Fetched: AISI English site (home, leadership, vision, organisation, policy, assessment, research, collaboration pages), AISI Korean home, KISA English and Korean homepages (200; no AISI mention found by title/menu scan, KISA about page /EN/about/sub01 returned 404), NIS homepage (200, JS shell with no text), plus one web search (ko, en) that returned only KISA-MSIT AI-security business programmes (2026-05) and no AISI link. The AISI policy page names "national security risk response" and "AI-induced vulnerabilities in national infrastructure" as tasks but names no cyber body; the AISI research page lists cybersecurity research only as a topic. The MSIT-Anthropic MOU (held kr-msit-anthropic-2026) is on AI safety and cybersecurity but names no cyber agency. Recorded as not published for the cyber domain, not as absence of any link.

testing_capacity.notes: Kakao says it carried out a joint safety evaluation of its own language model with the institute in 2025: '카카오는 지난해 인공지능안전연구소와 함께 자체 언어모델 'Kanana-1.5-9.8B'를 대상으로 공동 안전성 평가를 진행했으며' (last year Kakao, together with the AI Safety Institute, carried out a joint safety evaluation of its own language model Kanana-1.5-9.8B). Article 10(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the AI Basic Act lists '인공지능안전 관련 평가 시스템의 구축 및 운영' (building and operating AI safety evaluation systems) among the institute's tasks. Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise) and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise). On 3 November 2026 the institute said it had evaluated the harmfulness of two open-weight models against versions with their refusal training removed; it keeps the detailed results private and published only the SHA-256 hash of the report.

model_access.notes: No access event, legal power or agreement providing for access to, or evaluation of, the models of a developer that has a model in Epoch AI's frontier set was found. Access to a model outside Epoch AI's frontier set: Kakao, which has never had a model in that set, jointly evaluated Kanana-1.5-9.8B with the institute in 2025 (access type not stated), and under the MOU of 28 September 2026 '카카오는 AI 안전성 평가 대상이 되는 자사 AI 모델과 AI 에이전트를 제공하고' (Kakao provides its own AI models and AI agents to be evaluated for AI safety), starting with pre- and post-deployment evaluation of language models. The OpenAI agreement (17 June 2026) shares evaluation methods and benchmarks and provides for neither access to nor evaluation of OpenAI's models; the Anthropic MOU (announced 29 June 2026, signing date not stated) is the science ministry's agreement, under which the institute is to cooperate, not an agreement between the institute and Anthropic. The bilateral agent evaluation with Singapore used models through public APIs. No legal power: the fact-finding powers of Article 40 of the AI Basic Act sit with the Minister of Science and ICT, and Article 10(3) of the Enforcement Decree lets the institute request materials only from state bodies.

The recently established AI Safety Institute (AISI) should act as the main body responsible for guiding the safe and trusted development and use of AI in India.

The AISI should be involved in research, risk assessment, and capacity-building. It should test and evaluate AI systems for risks and provide advice to policymakers and industry actors on issues of AI safety.
Develop draft guidelines, codes, standards, respective evaluation metrics and testing frameworks in collaboration with relevant agencies and sectoral regulators.
The AISI should also anchor India’s participation in global forums and facilitate collaborations, such as in the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.

sources.title: Long-Form Tasks

excerpts.text: Long-Form Tasks
AISI has designed an evaluation methodology called a Long-Form Task (LFT) which aims to assess the model's ability to provide helpful instructions to a user in a scientific setting.

The core components of an LFT are (i) a prompt, which asks the LLM to generate detailed instructions to accomplish a high-level goal; and (ii) an autograder which uses a rubric written by domain experts to assign a score to the instructions provided.

sources.title: Our Research Agenda

excerpts.text: Our Research Agenda
By sharing AISI’s research agenda we intend to highlight priority risk domains and the solutions we are pursuing to address them;
This work includes close collaboration with the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

We develop threat models that map plausible scenarios of how threat actors may use frontier AI to support criminal activity that could harm UK citizens, in collaboration with the Home Office, National Security and law enforcement partners.

Working in collaboration with security partners and cross-government cyber experts such as National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) and Laboratory for AI Security Research (LASR), we aim to identify AI-driven cyber risk scenarios with potential to cause significant harm.
We conduct expert probing, where cyber experts prompt models to assess how much useful information can be extracted from them.

We will continue to evaluate and scan the horizon to ensure we focus our research on the most critical risks, one emerging area we are exploring is routes to help combat Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) risks stemming from both proprietary and open-source models.

Eine eigenständige Befugnis des AISI Deutschland, gegen den Willen von Entwicklern, Anbietern oder Betreibern fortgeschrittener KI-
Modelle Informationen oder Modellzugang zu verlangen, ist daher nicht vorge-
sehen.
excerpts.gloss: An independent power for AISI Deutschland to require information or model access against the wishes of developers, providers or operators of advanced AI models is therefore not envisaged.

excerpts.text: Soweit für technische Evaluierungen hoheitliche Informations- oder Zugriffsrechte erforderlich sind, richten sich diese nach den jeweils einschlägigen gesetzlichen Befugnissen der zuständigen Behörden, insbesondere nach der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-VO).
excerpts.gloss: Where public-authority information or access rights are required for technical evaluations, these follow the relevant statutory powers of the competent authorities in each case, in particular the European AI Regulation (KI-VO).

excerpts.text: Das AISI Deutschland unterliegt dabei insbesondere der parlamentarischen Kontrolle über die für seinen Aufbau und seine Steuerung zuständigen Ressorts. Ein eigenständiger regelmäßiger Bericht des AISI Deutschland an den Deutschen Bundestag ist nicht vorgesehen.
excerpts.gloss: AISI Deutschland is subject in particular to parliamentary scrutiny through the ministries responsible for its establishment and direction. No separate regular report by AISI Deutschland to the Bundestag is envisaged.

excerpts.text: Der weitere organisatorische, personelle und finanzielle Auf- und Ausbau des AISI Deutschland erfolgt schrittweise, ein konkreter Zeitpunkt für dessen Abschluss ist daher bislang nicht festgelegt.

changelog.summary: First public release. Each state's institute status and mandate, publications, funding, staff, leadership, national partners and source quotes, all downloadable as JSON and CSV.
changes: Covers all 193 UN member states plus Taiwan and the EU AI Office, with Europe in detail. For each state it records whether there is an institute, what it is meant to do, how it is set up, who it reports to and which national bodies it works with, with sources and the date on which each entry was last checked.

Lists each institute's publications and agreements, and shows its earliest published work and joint testing. When an institute was credited with a report later than the report appeared, both dates are shown.

Converts budgets to euros at the ECB's 2025 average rates and rounds them to two significant figures. The budget comparison counts only funding adopted or announced for the whole institute. Related funding and proposals are shown separately.
For states without an institute, says how sure we are. For some, it names the closest body and says why it does not count. AI Act authorities are listed separately from institutes.
Every claim cites its source, with source quotes and English translations of non-English source titles. Archive links are given where they exist.
Downloads in JSON and CSV, plus one file per state and per institute for scripts and agents.
Short method summaries on the page, with the full rules on a separate Method page. Figures from secondary sources, press reports or our own estimates are marked as such.
Code under MIT; data, page text and documentation under CC BY 4.0. Source quotes remain with their rights holders.

Records in the downloads and API whether a source states that an institute tests AI models, in house or through named other bodies, or plans to, and how it gets access to leading models: dated pre-release or deeper access, a legal power to require access, or an agreement with a developer that provides for access to, or evaluation of, its models, with quotations, Epoch AI's model data and dated search logs.

Gives the compared annual budget per person on the page, in the downloads and in the API, and its share of GDP in the downloads and API, using the recorded 2025 population and the World Bank's 2025 GDP in national currency.

Records how each institute is staffed (own staff, staff of existing bodies, a core team with partners, a unit in a host body, planned, or not published), each with a quotation from a source dated 2023 or later, in the downloads and the API.

changelog.summary: Corrections from a pre-launch accuracy check of the institute records, a re-check of 20 states with no institute identified, and clearer wording on the page.
changes: Japan: the institute now tests models itself. Its evaluation note of 2 October 2026 reports a June 2026 evaluation of Claude Opus 4.8 with the cyber safeguards removed, so testing reads In house and model access Yes. The note is added to its publications.

United States: earliest published work is now 17 January 2025, a technical blog on agent-hijacking evaluations by the institute's staff (then the U.S. AI Safety Institute), credited from the original version of the page.
Australia: earliest published work is now 10 August 2026, the institute's first publication, on risks and controls for multi-agent systems (research by Gradient Institute).
South Korea: staff of 38 as of October 2026, from a press report of the parliamentary audit; previously Not published.
Agreements added: the memorandum between the Canadian and Korean institutes of 8 July 2026, and the Korean institute's memorandum with Kakao of 28 September 2026.

National partners: entries that rested only on a list of participants or on past work, with no task assigned with the institute, are removed (Dstl in the United Kingdom, Viginum in France, eleven Japanese ministries and agencies, Nkom and the Data Protection Authority in Norway, which now reads Not published, and the Juvenile Prosecution Service in Spain).
Germany: the host is now the federation that the digital and interior ministries set up and task, as for France, so the member bodies are no longer also the host.
France: mandate texts now follow the founding announcement and the SGDSN page; the unsupported phrase on regulatory powers is removed.
Japan: the head's title is recorded as part-time, as published, and the staff target of 60 is attributed to the governing party's recommendation it comes from.
Malaysia: status confidence raised to high, because the ministry's release states the establishment.
EU AI Office: the staff record notes the lower figure on the AI Office's own page, and a note says the interval counts from the Commission decision of 24 January 2024.
Budgets: the US FY2026 note cites NIST's FY2027 request, which gives an existing CAISI base of USD 11m; the UK budget also cites the written answer of 15 October 2026.

Mandate and staff texts for the United Kingdom, Germany, Spain, Norway, the United States and South Korea reworded where they went beyond their sources, after a blind meaning check, with the supporting quotes bound.
Wording and source title corrections for Spain, Germany, the United Kingdom, South Korea and the United States.
Access notes record six cited pages whose live URLs now return 404 (among them NIST's May 2026 CAISI agreements announcement); their archived and retained copies remain the evidence.
Searched 20 states again for an institute that evaluates advanced models, in English and in national or official languages, with the limits recorded for Bhutan. None was found.

Raised confidence from low to medium for 13 of them (Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Sierra Leone, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Tunisia, United Arab Emirates), where primary sources on the national AI set-up are now cited; for Burkina Faso, French counts as a national or official language. The other 7 stay low, each with its reason recorded.

Page: the Network column says Not a member for states outside the international network instead of Not published; medium-confidence figures are labelled 'indirect or secondary'; a law is shown as the source of an institute's mandate ('mandate set by law').
Method: for budget and staff, Not published means that no figure was found in the sources checked.
Corrections: a report form on GitHub, prefilled from the page's correction links, and guidance for agents on answering from the data.

changelog.summary: The page opens on the world, the Atom feed carries News as well as new versions, every institute and the low-confidence states with no institute were checked again, and several institutes have new funding figures.
changes: Page: opens on the world, with region tabs over the map, less text and section addresses named by what readers see (#map, #testing, #funding, #news, #europe, #world, #data, #method); older addresses still work.
Page: larger type on wide screens; the theme follows the system unless you choose light or dark.
The Atom feed, feed.xml, now announces each News item as well as each new version, and News links to it.
Every institute is shown with the same fields whatever its status: Budget, Staff, Related funding and Institutional set-up now cover all 15. Norway shows its NOK 30m proposal and 12 to 15 staff.
All 15 institutes were checked again on 24 October 2026. New: the UK-Japan statement, the UK institute's more than 55 pre-release evaluations and Jade Leung as UK Vice-Chair.
Searched the 37 low-confidence states with no institute identified again: none qualifies, and 9 are now medium confidence.

Every state now has a planned re-check date in the downloads: every six months for states with an institute or a government step towards one, yearly where one is plausible, and on a two-year rotation for the rest.

United Kingdom: GBP 69m for 2025/26 and the GBP 120m Budget line. United States: the FY2027 request, now high confidence from the saved budget PDF. Canada: CAD 6m a year to CIFAR. Germany: EUR 81.2m in related funding.
Kenya: the KES 2,000m proposal. Amounts in a currency the ECB publishes no rate for stay in that currency and are not compared.

Germany: the institute's build-up as the government's answer of 19 October 2026 (21/8727) describes it. Qatar: cites the gazetted decision on the National AI Centre, confidence medium. Netherlands: exploring since 1 June 2026. Kazakhstan: kaisi.kz is no longer in the domain registry; the government designation remains unverified.

Canada: the co-directors of the CAISI Research Program now cite CIFAR's news post of 12 December 2024, since the CAISI newsroom no longer lists it. Spain: checked again on 4 November 2026, with no sign yet of the initial technical core.

Method: the definition, the Established status and the qualifying-body rule say "a national government or an international organisation, such as the EU"; a counterpart route needs an AI safety or model-evaluation remit in the same act; every rule uses one term, "general-purpose or frontier AI models"; "Why this bar" is now "Why testing, not size". 21 other rules are reworded for readability, with meaning unchanged.
Method: the None identified summary says states were searched in English and their official languages where possible. New glossary entry AISI; Taiwan's summary says why its testing does not count.
United States: one current name for the institute, with CAISI and US AI Safety Institute marked as former names.

Notes explain four dates: the United States institute is dated from its February 2024 confirmation, not the November 2023 announcement; India's 2025 rests on one phrase in the November 2025 guidelines; no dated source gives the United Kingdom institute's move to the Cabinet Office; the network's founding date is the US fact sheet's 20 November 2024, while the members' mission statement says 21 November.
The budget median says when it is a ceiling, the world table counts states and territories, and Chad's offline UNECA workshop page links to its archived copy.

changelog.summary: Euros for every amount with an ECB rate; all 193 states in the region lists; Cmd+K search; wording revised throughout; corrections to Norway's staff and Canada's funding period.
changes: Page: every amount in a currency with an ECB reference rate is also shown in euros, followed by the stated amount, whether or not it is compared. Amounts in other currencies, such as the Kenyan shilling, stay in that currency. The euro figures are computed on the page; the downloads add no new fields.

Page: the Europe view also lists the 12 European states outside the European scope, under "Elsewhere in Europe, not in the European counts", so the region lists cover all 193 states. The European counts still cover the same 32 states.
Page: Cmd+K (Ctrl+K) opens a search that jumps to any state, institute or section.
Page: shorter tooltips, no repeated labels or explanations, sentences instead of fragments, one focus style, fewer lines, clearer map contrast and phone layout fixes.
Page: "No privileged access found" now says which access it means; the figures note names what its numbers count; English translations appear beside non-English source titles.
Norway: the funding row shows the 12 to 15 staff the card shows. Canada: the budget period reads 2024-25 to 2028-29. India and Malaysia: Form reads "Not published; set up by administrative act".
Page: partners whose description only says they are partners show by name. The US, Japan and Korea staff notes say the source gives the count as current in that month.

State summaries, AI Act authority descriptions, closest candidates and funding notes rewritten as sentences that lead with what was found; legal references spelled out. Finland and Ireland name their single points of contact; Slovenia's authorities state their own remits; Kenya's funding note says its plan gives no start for the 0 to 24 months.
Method: the currency rule says plainly that only amounts with an ECB rate are shown in euros.

Downloads: no fields added or removed. institutes[].display.intervals.status_since now also carries the announcement date when the interval to establishment is not exact ("Announced on 25 Nov 2025"), and several summaries, descriptions and notes have new wording.

changelog.summary: New outputs, notes and access events for the UK, US, Korea, Japan and other institutes from a re-check of their news on 7 November; Italy's AI Act authorities under Legislative Decree 179/2026; partners that share an explanation listed together; a page title and description that say what the tracker covers.
changes: Indonesia: AISII's role names KORIKA as an independent membership association, from KORIKA's report of its first members' meeting of 2026.

UK: two research outputs (ReproBAIT; pretraining data filtering in protein language models), the 2025-26 compute spend in the funding notes and the UK-Japan Frontier Technology Partnership of 14 June 2026 as an agreement, also on Japan's card.

Korea: ROK-FORTRESS (with Scale AI, credited from 18 September 2026) and the Korean edition of the Frontier AI Risk Update as outputs; the evaluation the institute reported on 3 November 2026, with results withheld, as in-house testing.
Japan: the institute's GLM-5.3 cyber capability evaluation of 30 October 2026 as an output; its models were used via API, with no access beyond that described, so no access event.

US: three research-blog posts as outputs (cheating on agent evaluations, transcript analysis, red-teaming competition insights); the reporting-line notes report a White House statement, reported by Semafor, on the Super Intelligence Force.
Canada: testing capacity records the National Research Council as testing models through the institute, from the council's AI safety page.

Germany: the notes cite BSI's monthly digests (not counted as outputs) and the AI taskforce report of 2 November 2026, with its plan for a second build-up phase and its target that the institute assess at least 75 per cent of new frontier models within four months.

Norway: KI Norge's mandate follows the wording of the budget bill (Prop. 1 S), which adds knowledge of the consequences and risks of advanced AI and names research communities and other actors as partners.

Italy: Legislative Decree 179/2026 (in force 23 October 2026) is now the designation basis of the AI Act authorities; the Banca d'Italia, CONSOB and IVASS have their own sectors, and the Garante is added for Article 74(8) uses. Law 132/2025 stays as history.
Bulgaria: the notes record that the parliamentary committee on innovation rejected the AI bill at first reading on 4 November 2026; its authority allocations stay proposals.
Hungary: the AI market surveillance authority operates as a unit of the Ministry of Science and Technology, its website says.

UK: adds the Gemini 4 Argon access event, dated 30 September 2026 (Google's announcement and Epoch AI's release date), with its limited first rollout to trusted cyber defenders and trusted testers in the notes.
News and publications of all 15 institutes re-checked on 7 November 2026, each with a dated note of what was read.
Page: partners that share an explanation are listed once under it, each name with its citation (Spain, the US, France, Japan and Canada).
Page: the (i) notes say what a section is; the Set-up and Funding scope notes are plain sentences.
Page: the title and description name AI safety and security institutes. The saved map is a separate file, so search engines index the whole page, and the sitemap lists pages only.
Downloads: no fields added or removed.

changelog.summary: Staff and budget notes for Canada, France and the EU AI Office, Canada's CIFAR research stream from 2024-25, Singapore's Digital Trust Centre grant period, four laws verified in force against official records, and official copies for Russia's and Ethiopia's laws.

changelog.summary: Plainer definition wording; Tajikistan's AI strategy confirmed in force; Grenada's Digital Transformation Agency Act cited from the published Act; a faster page and map.
changes: Definition: the last sentence now reads "Being a regulator, certification body or cyber security agency is not enough on its own." The rule is unchanged.

changelog.summary: The UK institute's funding is now one £360m record for 2026-27 to 2029-30, and its corrected staff count is 243. Updates also cover AI Act authorities on the EU's contact list of 9 November 2026, Malaysia, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, El Salvador, Norway, the United States and Ecuador, with replaced sources for moved pages.
changes: United Kingdom: funding is one whole-institute record of £360m for 2026-27 to 2029-30, the £240m Spending Review allocation plus £120m from Budget 2026, from a written answer of 6 November 2026. No source splits it by year, so it is compared at its four-year mean of £90m a year; the £240m and £120m are its components and are not counted twice.
United Kingdom: staff are 243 (227.8 full-time equivalent) as at 12 October 2026, 109 in technical and 134 in other roles; the written answer was corrected on 22 October from 241.

United Kingdom: the notes add, from written answers, that there is no fixed frontier threshold, that all current collaboration agreements are with UK and US developers and that results are not typically published.
Malaysia: the mandate adds safety benchmarking, risk assessment and incident reporting for corrective action, from the Digital Minister's answer in the Dewan Rakyat on 5 October 2026.

EU AI Act authorities, from the Commission's contact list of 9 November 2026: Germany and Slovenia are no longer marked pending there (their designations already rested on national acts); Hungary's related body is now the Minister of Science and Technology, and the notes record that Decree 224/2026 repealed section 5(1)(e) of Decree 344/2025; Bulgaria and Slovakia are listed but stay proposed, as a list entry is not a designation. Notes for ten states still marked pending now cite the updated list date.
Republic of the Congo: Law 14-2024 of 23 May 2024 creates the African Research Centre for AI, now named by its French acronym CARIA (previously ARCAI); it has no task to test or evaluate AI models.
Equatorial Guinea: the notes name Óscar Ondo Ngomo as Secretary of State responsible for AI Systems under Decree 61/2026.
El Salvador: Legislative Decree 674 (Diario Oficial No. 178, 25 September 2026) on national AI and robotics projects is recorded; it neither amends nor repeals Resolution 0001/2025.
Norway: KI Norge's staffing notes record a consultant contracted as executive assistant to its management (contract award of 22 October 2026).
United States: the institute's research agreement with Scale AI, announced on 10 February 2025, is added, now that NIST's March 2026 update lists Scale AI among its agreements.

Ecuador: the National Assembly's records are now cited first: the unified AI bill was archived on 15 September 2026, and an AI-governance bill was admitted on 28 September and referred to the Education Committee.

Chad: the ministry's own report and organisation chart are now cited first; the summary says the ministry lists a General Directorate for AI, with an organisation decree of September 2025 per the ministry and a reorganisation in October 2025 reported by Tchadinfos.
Kazakhstan: the closest-body note now cites Harvard's 2026 hackathon page and says that operations after the domain's removal are unconfirmed.

Sources for moved or changed pages: Georgia, Turkmenistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina, Italy's Law 132/2025 (now cited from the Gazzetta Ufficiale), Japan's 2023 commitment, METR, NIST's May 2026 agreements and the Commission's Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755.
The news re-checks of 9 November 2026 covered all 15 institutes.

changelog.summary: Australia's institute now records five national partners and a policy output, the Rapid Review into government arrangements for an AI-driven cyber incident, and a new rule counts technical staff, giving Korea at least 6 and Australia about 12. Updates also cover the EU's ENISA, Poland's NASK and OpenAI agreement, the Paris Call signatories and Cyprus.
changes: Method: a rule for technical staff counts. A stated count or a share of a stated total is used; a count derived from a share is marked about or at least, with the figures it comes from, and the rule says which partial or approximate figures give no count. Korea's institute now records at least 6 technical staff and Australia's about 12 of its 25.

Method: source preference asks for the primary text itself, quoted in its original language, or an archived copy of the issuer's page with an access note when the page cannot be retrieved; another country's account alone is allowed only when no source from the state itself was found or retrieved.

Australia: the Rapid Review into Australian Government arrangements for an AI-driven cyber incident, released on 10 November 2026 and undertaken by PM&C in collaboration with agencies including the institute, is recorded as an output that is not published evaluation work.

Australia: PM&C, the National Cyber Security Coordinator (a role supported by the National Office of Cyber Security), the Office of AI, Services Australia and DFAT are added as partners, and the notes record the proposed AI safety regulator.

EU: ENISA is added as a related body. A Commission spokesperson said on 11 September 2026 that the Commission had official access to Anthropic's Mythos 5 and that ENISA was testing it; the press reported that Anthropic had agreed in principle in June, that the access was limited to defensive use and that it did not cover Mythos 5.1.
United Kingdom: the institute's own network page is a second source for the ten International Network memberships.
Korea: Money Today is a second source for the six technical evaluators, and the notes add its report that the institute uses outside GPU resources.

Poland: NASK's agreement with OpenAI on AI safety research (23 October 2026), to be led by the centre NASK describes as the Polish AI Safety Institute, is in the notes; Poland stays at none identified, as no government act assigns a national evaluation role.
Poland: CERT Polska's access to OpenAI cyber models since July is in the notes.
Poland: KRiBSI held its first meeting on 28 October.
Hungary: press reports of its proposed EU Frontier AI Safety and Security Team are in the notes.
Hungary: the AI Act wording is corrected.
Hungary: the AI Council's first meeting now cites the Council's declaration.
Hungary: Decree 90/2026's status is checked.
Iceland: the notes record that Umbra and CERT-IS received access to an OpenAI cyber security model for defensive cyber work.

Paris Call for AI Safety and Security of 9 November 2026: a sentence in the notes of the eleven signatory states without an institute (Austria, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Portugal).
Proposals that are not the government's own get a dated note and no status change: Romania's bill B597/2026, Brazil's bill PL 5960/2025 and the French expert commission's report on INESIA.
Cyprus: the cabinet approved the 2026-2032 national AI strategy on 10 November.
Switzerland: the consultation on legislation implementing the Council of Europe AI Convention is now planned for spring 2027.
Czechia: the government approved the AI Act implementation bill and set up a Government Council for AI.
Netherlands: the cabinet's AI vision of 6 November repeats that it is exploring an AI safety institute.
Finland: the notes record the Finland-Norway leaders' meeting on frontier AI control and its follow-up expert process.
Austria: the notes record the proposed UN centre for AI cooperation in Vienna.
South Africa: the notes record the timetable for the revised national AI policy.
Brazil: ANPD finished its first AI sandbox and is preparing a second, on digital games for children and adolescents.
El Salvador, Djibouti and Botswana: roles and notes now say only what their sources say.
India: the unsupported Hindi local name is removed.
Italy: the current status of Law 132/2025 article 20 could not be verified, and its status check date is left unset.
Notes for Australia's partners, INESIA and the Netherlands no longer name retrieval tools or people.
Partial news re-checks of 10 November 2026 are recorded for all 15 institutes and the 40 EU, OECD and G20 states without an institute, with what was read and what could not be.

changelog.summary: The UK's institute and Norway's KI Norge are named in a 12 November statement of intent to explore cooperation on AI security and testing. Russia's new decree on large foundation models is in the notes.
changes: United Kingdom and Norway: the joint statement of intent on AI signed in Oslo on 12 November 2026, which names the UK institute and KI Norge for exploring cooperation, is recorded as a non-binding agreement on both records, cited from the signed text the UK government published.
Korea: the notes record the AI Safety Guardians, 80 people selected from 138 applicants to find and report AI errors and risks, launched by the science ministry and the institute on 12 November 2026.

Russia: government decree 1461 of 6 November 2026, which adds the analysis of large foundation AI models and related support and incentive measures to the digital development ministry's powers, is in the notes.
Finland: the government's bill HE 270/2026 of 22 October 2026, under which Traficom would set up and run the AI regulatory sandbox, is in the notes.
Romania: bill B597/2026 is no longer marked as legal text, as it is not an adopted instrument.
Slovenia: the AI Competence Centre (KCUI) is recorded as operating as the national AI hub, as the government's page says, no longer as planned.
Bulgaria: the INSAIT entry now cites INSAIT's own site and no longer names a university affiliation that no source supports.
Kenya: the notes call the institute's status planned, as recorded.
Page: the command palette offers the light, dark and system themes as separate actions.
Partial news re-checks of 13 November 2026 are recorded for all 15 institutes, with what was read and what could not be.

changelog.summary: Every status change now carries a quote from a primary source, with one listed exception. Among the corrections, the Maldives' lead body is now the Maldives Digital Service.
changes: Method: a new rule, primary evidence for status changes. Every act that moves a status, and every launch date, now carries a quote from a primary source; a primary source published on the act's date carries that date. The one exception is Korea's commitment of 22 May 2024, for which no government text of the minister's remarks was found; its source says what was searched.

Maldives: the National Centre for Information Technology was abolished on 15 January 2026; the Maldives Digital Service, which took over its responsibilities, is now the related body, cited from the President's Office.
Antigua and Barbuda: the UNESCO readiness assessment is recorded as completed, as a July 2026 regional report says.
Bulgaria: the AI Act bill was rejected at first reading in committee on 4 November 2026. Cyprus: the national AI strategy was approved on 10 November 2026.
United States: the institute's current name is dated by NIST's own page as archived on 30 September 2026, not 3 October.

Wording narrowed to what the cited sources say, in the summaries, notes or related bodies of Australia, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Canada, the Central African Republic, Estonia, France, Haiti, Iraq, Kuwait, Lesotho, Luxembourg, Madagascar, Malta, Norway, Oman, Pakistan, Paraguay, Romania, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saudi Arabia, Trinidad and Tobago and Tunisia.
Bills: each bill described gives its latest formal step with its date (Brazil, Finland, Mexico, Bulgaria).

European related bodies: every one now cites a source, among them Austria's AI service desk, Liechtenstein's digital innovation office, Luxembourg's and Romania's AI Factories and Greece's AI coordination centre and sandbox; names no longer carry a stage, which is in the role with a quote (Bulgaria, Cyprus, Iceland).

AI Act authorities: the designation state of the authorities in 24 countries is now quoted, from the Commission's list of 9 November 2026 or from the national act or account where the list has no entry, names only the contact point or differs from the act. One Romanian authority, the notifying authority ADR, has no quote for its state yet.
Partial news re-checks of 14 November 2026 are recorded for all 15 institutes, with what was read and what could not be.

changelog.summary: A new Functions table compares the mandates and activities of the 15 institutes across 18 functions. News now also covers changes of mandate or name, budget decisions and agreements.
changes: Functions: a new table under Compare. For each of the 15 institutes it shows which of 18 functions are part of its mandate and which it carries out. The functions are shown in four groups, with all 18 one click away. A mark opens the claim and its source, and the quote opens from there.

Functions: the table rests on 163 claims, each with a quote from a public source: 99 on mandates and 64 on activities. We found no text for any institute on capacity building or on access and continuity for public bodies.

Functions in the data: new files functions.csv and claims.csv, and new fields `functions` and `claims` for each institute in aisi.json and the API. The function codes and the two `development` codes (public_body, testing_duty) are provisional: a minor version may add, split, rename or remove them, and the changelog will say so.

Claims: 242 facts on the page are now one-sentence claims with a quote from the source. They cover the Functions table, facts on the cards, what related bodies do and the closest body's main quote. A translated quote is shown in English, with the original on hover, focus or tap. In the data, each quote and claim has the date we last found it in its source.
News: besides changes of status, News now lists changes of mandate or name, budget decisions for the institute itself, and agreements. Each entry says in one sentence what happened.

Downloads: new file news.csv with the News entries; an agreement between two states has one row per state. events.csv gains the columns news_kind and news. Functions, the other comparison tables and News each have a download link below them.

Downloads, other new columns: anchors in source_excerpts.csv; designation_step_text and designation_step_date in related_bodies.csv; body_id and active_in in closest_bodies.csv. No file, column or code was removed or renamed.
Method: two new rules, on bills and on News. Each function's definition and test are in the vocabulary `function`.

Method: the rules on budget display, national partners and states with no institute identified now say what is shown, not where on the page. The partners rule no longer says a card shows six partners.

Europe: the summary for each of the 32 European states is now generated from the record's fields and quoted claims, and the notes under How we checked from its check dates and searches. They replace the earlier written notes. Facts from those notes that the record holds nowhere else are no longer shown.
Summaries: the generated summaries for the UK, France and Germany now give the founding date and the present form in separate sentences.

Related bodies removed: the innovation ministry as a separate body in Bulgaria, the digital ministry in Croatia, four planned bodies in Cyprus, the centre for AI and language technology in Iceland, the KTU centre of excellence in Lithuania, the sandbox configurator in Luxembourg, the AI Factory in Romania and the SIMULAB lab in Slovakia. Greece's sandbox is now a role of EETT and the data protection authority, not a body of its own.

Closest bodies: for China, Cyprus, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Mozambique, Poland, Slovakia, Taiwan and the United Arab Emirates, the closest body now has quoted claims about what it does or is meant to do. For Cyprus, Poland and Slovakia the summary names it and gives its main quote.
Norway: the 2027 budget proposal is NOK 45.1m for KI Norge as a whole. The NOK 30m for evaluating AI models and studying risks is part of that sum.
South Korea: 12 staff as at 27 November 2024, from the ministry's release. The director was appointed on 12 November 2024.
EU AI Office: a funding record says that no amount is published for the Office as a whole, and names the budget lines in the Commission decision of 24 January 2024.
United Kingdom: the Gemini 4 Argon access event is dated 13 October 2026, not 30 September.
Australia: the short mandate now reads "emerging AI capabilities and risks", from the institute's page as re-read on 16 November 2026.

United States and Japan: the designation events of February 2024 now cite the governments' own announcements. The US event of 30 September 2026 says the institute was renamed from the Center for AI Standards and Innovation.
People: professional backgrounds added for the heads or named officials of eight institutes: the United Kingdom, Norway, the EU AI Office, the United States, Canada, Japan, South Korea and Singapore.
Bulgaria: the twelve AI Act authorities are no longer marked as proposed. INSAIT's role is its EXPLORER talent programme.

Quoted facts added: Norway (Digdir's interim organisation for KI Norge from 1 December 2025), Japan (Kenji Hiramoto took office as full-time secretary-general on 14 February 2024), the EU AI Office (its first job announcement), India (the call for one contract director), Poland (cooperation between NASK's centre and Korea's institute), Taiwan (131 model tests by its evaluation centre, as reported on 4 May 2026) and Indonesia (the planned AISII Academy).
Sweden: the follow-up on the AI Commission's institute recommendation moves from 13 to 20 November 2026.

Notes on funding, testing, model access and staffing for the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Spain, Norway and the EU AI Office now say only what their quotes support. No classification of testing, model access or staffing changed.

Sources: 15 added, 1,272 in total. 26 English translations of quotes corrected. Eight sources that were offline on 16 November 2026 are marked as offline, with an archived copy where one exists. Source lists show when a source was last re-read, where recorded.

Page: per-person figures in the funding chart are labelled per resident, with the population year. Lists of five or more bodies, members or partners show three and a count. Source titles are shown in English where we have a translation, with the original on hover, focus or tap. Table heads and the head of an open record stay visible while you scroll.

Checks recorded since 1.0.10: searches for Poland (15 November 2026) and Norway (17 November); the Australian institute's page re-read (16 November); source quotes re-read on 10 and 16 November. No record's full-check date changed.

changelog.summary: Funding and staff is now two bar charts of established institutes, Budget and Staff. Corrections include Australia's launch on 1 June 2026 and staff of 29, staffing models for India and Norway, and four Functions cells.
changes: Funding and staff are two bar charts of established institutes, Budget and Staff, each on its own scale with one line per institute. Period, date and qualifications are in each figure's explanation and in the records.
Institutes without a published or comparable figure are named in a line under each chart; opening the line lists them and leads to their records.
Kenya, Norway and Spain, whose institutes are not yet established, are no longer in Funding and staff. Their amounts stay on their cards, in their records and in the downloads.
Australia: the timeline gains the institute's launch on 1 June 2026, from the industry department's annual report. The assistant minister called it operational the next day.

Australia: the institute had 29 staff (27.4 full-time equivalent) on 29 October 2026, seven of them evaluating models, from the uncorrected proof Hansard of a Senate estimates hearing. The model access notes add that hearing's account: the institute reaches Anthropic models through its technical partners while the technical side of access under its MOUs is worked out.

Australia: the network's best practice guidance on automated evaluation, to which Australia contributed through the institute, is now in the catalogue. It is the first output credited to the institute (24 July 2026); its earliest published work reporting results stays 10 August 2026.

Australia: the Rapid Review entry now also cites the full report of 20 November 2026. A new fact from it: OpenAI held its first technical exchange with the institute and three other agencies on 22 September 2026.
India: the institute's staffing model is now "unit in a host body". Its host, Digital India Corporation, recruits the Director and team; the partner cells are described in the notes.

Norway: KI Norge's staffing model is now "unit in a host body": Digdir's report calls it a department of Digdir with permanent and loaned staff. The communications authority Nkom and the data protection authority Datatilsynet are listed as planned partners for Norway's regulatory AI sandbox.

Norway and the United Kingdom: the statement of intent of 12 November 2026 now cites, for Norway, the Norwegian government's own release, which calls it a letter of intent signed with a view to a later memorandum of understanding. Both records add the UK government's answer of 19 November that no dedicated funding has been allocated under it.
United States: International cooperation now reads "activity". The 2023 founding announcement, which the 2025 statement replaced, no longer counts as a current assignment.
Canada: Standards and guidelines now reads "not found". The institute's statement that it provides guidance stays in the record as a fact.
United Kingdom: Research now rests on the institute's assignment only, no longer on activity as well. Funding Epoch AI's work on predictions stays in the record as a fact.
Spain: Policy advice now reads "not found". The plan's "technical advice to the General State Administration" names no policy subject and stays as a fact.
Singapore: the research assignment now names the two safety research areas, without testing and governance. No value changes.

United Kingdom: the event of 14 February 2025 is now recorded as a new name, not a change of mandate. Its text says what the release says: the institute is renamed, a criminal misuse team is announced, it will not focus on bias or freedom of speech, and the minister says its work will not change. In News it reads "Government renames the institute and announces a criminal misuse team."

United Kingdom: the reporting line notes a written answer of 18 November 2026, by which two Directors lead the institute and report to the Director General for Artificial Intelligence. The answer names neither; the recorded head is unchanged.

United Kingdom: the model access notes add three accounts of 2026. A House of Commons committee report of 18 November says the institute has no statutory right of access to models. The institute's Director wrote on 15 September that no organisation outside the US had access to Mythos 5.1 at its release. Anthropic says it could not give access without safeguards before deployment then, and has since given it for its latest models.

United Kingdom: the testing notes add, from written answers of 16 and 18 November 2026, that the institute does not test models specifically for child safety risks and does not report on compliance with the Online Safety Act or on copyright. A new fact records the AI Threat Assessment Centre, which draws on the institute's expertise. The pay range and pension contribution now carry quotes.

Thailand: the note on the draft AI law is corrected. Its committee is the existing committee for the national AI plan, not a new one; comments on draft principles ran until 24 June 2025 and a hearing on the full draft from 9 July to 14 August 2026; on 7 September 2026 the committee resolved that restructuring of the draft be considered.

United Arab Emirates: the remarks of October 2026 on independent testing are now attributed to Khaleej Times of 6 October and to an adviser to the UAE President, who spoke of countries in general. The unsourced sentence "Closest case in the region" is removed. The AI and data authority is described in its announcement's words: it brings together functions previously held by three entities.

Saudi Arabia: the note on the draft Responsible AI Policy now follows the policy text. Consultation ran until 3 May 2026; the draft would require comprehensive safety tests before a high-risk system is released and annual audits by an accredited third party; it was still a draft on 4 November 2026.

Iraq: Article 13 of the draft regulation applies to providers or operators of general-purpose models; all 19 articles have now been read. Oman: the note adds the Cabinet's approval of the national AI programme on 19 September 2024 and the international centre for AI ethics and governance planned for 2026 to 2030, which has no testing task.

Netherlands: the next check moves from 16 November to 31 December 2026; the advisory report on a Dutch AI safety institute is expected in parliament in December 2026. Poland: the minister's role as notifying authority is now quoted from the Polish law, and the next check notes that the AI commission KRiBSI first met on 28 October 2026.
Italy: Article 20 of Law 132/2025 is unchanged since it came into force, by the consolidated text on Normattiva as it stood on 20 November 2026.
Definitions: "works with" for national partners now matches the method: a text in force assigns the partner a specific task with the institute.
Sources: 25 added, 1,297 in total. One quoted heading corrected (Malaysia).

Page: a panel opened from a table or the map names the state first, then the institute, and that head stays in view while you scroll. A panel opened from one cell of the full Functions table also keeps the function's name.
Page: tables, charts and their notes now end at the same edge, and running text keeps a shorter line.
Page: no line begins with a separator dot.
Page: a selected row or cell is marked by a tint and an accent bar.
Page: quotes stored with line breaks are now shown with them; 36 quotes have such breaks.

Page: "Definition" under the headline shows the definition on hover, focus and tap. The close mark on cards and panels is larger, a card's download sits at the right edge, and a table head that stays in view keeps its space above.
Downloads: the descriptions of eleven files are shorter and say what each file is, for example "A plain-text guide to the data for AI agents" for llms.txt.

Checks recorded since 1.1.0: the news check of 20 November 2026 for all 15 institutes and partial checks of 19 November for Iraq, the Netherlands, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Thailand and the United Arab Emirates. No record's full-check date changed.

changelog.summary: Estonia's closest body is now shown, Germany and Japan's announced cooperation is recorded, and facts in a record carry the date of their source. Corrections to source lists and three notes.
changes: Estonia: the Secure AI Knowledge Centre initiative (T3) of the Estonian Academy of Security Sciences is shown as the closest body. Estonia's status is unchanged: no qualifying institute identified.

Germany and Japan: the two governments' leaders announced on 28 October 2026 that they will explore cooperation on AI safety and security through their institutes. Both records list it as an announced agreement.
EU AI Office: the short mandate now reads "Enforces the AI Act's rules for general-purpose AI models; evaluates those with systemic risk."
EU AI Office: its draft template for fundamental rights impact assessments of 16 November 2026 is in the catalogue, as guidance.
Germany: the note on related funding no longer opens with "Related funding."
Malaysia and China: two notes no longer contain wording meant for editors.
Sources: three sources that were listed twice are now listed once (the network's best practice guidance on automated evaluation, Singapore's resources page and Korea's collaboration page).
Sources: a web page's title is now its own heading, not the site's name. Five titles corrected, among them two CyberSecurity Malaysia pages that both read "CyberSecurity Malaysia".
Sources: 9 added, 1,303 in total.
Method: the rule on source titles says how two sources that would read the same line are told apart. The page adds each one's language, or else its web host.

Page: a fact in a record shows the date of its earliest source, so an older fact no longer reads as current. A fact whose sentence already names that year, or whose source has no publication date, shows none.
Page: in a funding record, the source type and date sit on their own line above the notes.
Page: the Closest body block no longer repeats the name and stage when the summary gives them.
Page: a qualifier line that wraps keeps its separator dot at the end of the first line.
Checks recorded since 1.1.1: the news check of 23 November 2026 for all 15 institutes and a partial check of 23 November for Estonia. No record's full-check date changed.

changelog.summary: The Functions view now shows since when an institute has done each kind of work, and its latest example. Twenty examples were added, and 130 sentences were reworded to say plainly what each institute does.
changes: Functions: for work an institute carries out, the page now says "active since at least" a date and shows the latest example. The date is that of the oldest published text in which we found the work. It is left out where we know of older work that we have not added yet.

Functions: an opened function shows when the task was assigned and since when the institute has been active. Below that it lists the assignment and the three most recent examples, each with its date and source; older ones sit under "earlier". The general definition of the function is no longer repeated there.

20 examples added, from sources the tracker already cited: the United Kingdom (7), the United States (6), Canada (2), Singapore (2), the EU AI Office (2) and South Korea (1). Among them are the joint evaluation of an Anthropic model by the UK and US institutes, the US evaluation of GLM-5.3, and the joint test by the Korean and Singapore institutes of whether AI agents leak sensitive data.
Functions: the UK's research, the EU AI Office's standards and guidelines, and Canada's model testing and research now read Active, not only assigned.

130 sentences reworded. A sentence now says what the institute does or was tasked with, and the source mark shows who published it. It names a speaker only where someone other than the publisher speaks, and starts with "It says" where an institute describes its work only in general terms.
Downloads and API: each institute's `functions` rows and `functions.csv` gain `since` and `newest`. In `claim_ids`, assignments come first, then examples, newest first.
Sources: publication dates added for six sources, each taken from the source itself. 1,303 sources in total, none added.

changelog.summary: Function entries that did not meet the function's test were removed or replaced for 11 institutes, and nine tasks now read not found. France, Canada, Japan and South Korea gain international cooperation entries from the network's joint multilingual testing.
changes: Functions: 25 entries that did not meet their function's test were removed, for Australia, the EU AI Office, France, Germany, Japan, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, South Korea, the United Kingdom and the United States: examples that did not show the institute doing the work, and assignments that rested on a plan item, a power rather than a task, the institute's own plans or another actor. One French example, a judge prompt designed for the network's joint agentic testing, now counts as evaluation methods instead of model testing.

Functions: nine tasks now read "not found": the United Kingdom's support for regulators; Germany's adoption, evaluation methods and research; the EU AI Office's regulatory sandbox; Japan's incident role; South Korea's adoption; and Malaysia's evaluation methods and certification.

Functions: 12 functions now read assigned, no longer active, because no remaining example shows the work: Australia (support for regulators, risk monitoring), the EU AI Office (risk monitoring), France (convening, support for regulators, research), Malaysia (incident role, risk monitoring), Norway (adoption), Singapore (research), South Korea (convening) and the United Kingdom (risk monitoring). Japan's convening keeps its example and no longer reads assigned.

Functions: France, Canada, Japan and South Korea gain international cooperation entries from their own sections of the network's report on joint multilingual testing; each now reads active since at least June 2025. France also gains a model testing example. The United States now reads active for standards and guidelines, from its draft guidelines for developers on managing misuse risk (NIST AI 800-1, July 2024), and its adoption example is now its work with the General Services Administration on federal procurement (since March 2026).

Functions: seven entries reworded to say what the source shows: the United Kingdom's alignment evaluation, the French judge prompt, the EU AI Office's AI Pact and GenAI4EU, now plain statements, South Korea's AI Safety Forecast Report, Australia's risk monitoring task ("is to" instead of "is being set up to"), and Malaysia's risk monitoring task, which now names the Ministry of Digital as publisher of the national AI action plan.

Method: a function reads active only where a source shows the institute's own work on it: a named piece of work or programme, or work the source reports as done. A statement of what an institute is for, focuses on or plans to do is at most an assigned task. The download schema and the API text say so.

United Kingdom: Pawan Mudigonda is added as Research Director, from the institute's About page of 24 November 2026. Jade Leung's note adds that she is Security Adviser to the AI Taskforce and was the Prime Minister's AI Adviser. The staffing description drops the employer pension figure, which the job advert no longer states.
Canada: the testing note now says that Canada tested two models in the network's joint multilingual testing; the joint agentic testing credits it with analysis.

Sources: a source that is offline now links to its archived copy wherever the page cites it; downloads and the API keep the source's own address. South Korea's AI Basic Act, Article 12, now links to a working address. A Norwegian source is now titled by what it is, Digdir's annual report for 2025. 1,303 sources, none added.

Downloads and API: an output can now carry `functions`, the codes of the functions it shows, judged on its source. 32 of 136 outputs carry it so far; an output without it is not yet judged. The new field is listed in `dataset.provisional`, so it may still change in a minor release.
Singapore: the network's best-practice document on automated evaluation is no longer listed among its outputs; the institute hosts it, and no source says it contributed. 136 outputs in total.
